name: Should you refinish existing hardwood floors or replace them in a foreclosure?

mainEntity.name: Should you refinish existing hardwood floors or replace them in a foreclosure?

acceptedAnswer.text: In many foreclosed properties, complete replacement is more practical and cost-effective than refinishing. While existing hardwoods add character, foreclosures often suffer from deep pet urine stains, cupping from standing water, or localized structural rotting that sanding cannot eliminate. Refinishing also takes time to cure properly. If only isolated patches are damaged, selective board replacement and restaining may work. However, if water or neglect has penetrated deep into the wood grain, installing resilient luxury vinyl or fresh tile avoids lingering smells and yields a uniform appearance across adjoining rooms.
acceptedAnswer.description: Replace the flooring if there is deep water damage or pet odor saturation. Refinishing works only if wood damage is strictly surface-level across the home.
